The platform is a trading journal web application built for retail traders to track, analyse, and improve their performance. The standout feature is an AI Trade Analyzer: users upload a screenshot of their trade (from any broker or exchange), and the AI extracts the trade details automatically — symbol, entry/exit price, quantity, date/time, and profit or loss — removing the need for manual data entry.

A key requirement is currency accuracy: since users may trade on Indian platforms (₹) or international/crypto platforms ($), the AI engine correctly detects and tags the currency for every trade, so P&L and analytics are never mixed up between Dollars and Rupees.
Central overview screen showing account summary, recent trades, P&L snapshot, and key performance widgets at a glance.
New-trader signup flow paired with the AI engine that reads uploaded trade screenshots and automatically extracts trade details, flagging unusual/anomalous entries for review.
Performance analytics — win rate, average R:R, P&L trends, drawdown, and instrument/strategy-wise breakdowns.
Ranks traders by performance metrics to drive engagement and friendly competition among users.
Tracks rule-following behaviour (stop-loss respected, overtrading, revenge trading, etc.) and scores trading discipline over time.
Account, notification, and preference management for each user.
Notification/messaging system between the platform and users, including message resend and unsend (recall) capability.
Full create, read, update, and delete control over logged trades, with support for manual entry and edits.
Internal dashboard to manage users, review flagged trades, moderate the leaderboard, and handle subscriptions and disputes.

Lets a user add up to two trading accounts (e.g. an equity account and a crypto account) and switch between them from one screen, with each account's trade history, analytics, and discipline score kept separate.
AI Trade Analyzer — How It Works
This is the platform's core differentiator. For every uploaded trade screenshot, the engine will:
Read the image and identify the broker/exchange layout it came from.
Extract the instrument/symbol, entry price, exit price, quantity, timestamp, and resulting P&L.
Detect whether the amounts are in ₹ (INR) or $ (USD), and tag every trade correctly.
Flag unusual entries (e.g. an outsized loss, an odd lot size, a duplicate) for the trader to double-check.
Feed clean, structured data into the Dashboard, Analytics, and Discipline Board automatically.
Tiered plans (free + paid) gating premium features such as the AI analyzer and advanced analytics.
Integrated checkout supporting Razorpay and UPI for Indian users.
Additional integration to accept payments via MetaMask and other crypto wallets, for global and crypto-native traders.
Usage limits and rate-limiting per plan tier to keep the platform fair and cost-efficient to run.
The core vision/AI model that reads trade screenshots, extracts structured trade data (symbol, entry/exit, quantity, date, P&L) and detects the correct currency automatically.
Backend, database, and API architecture design to support the AI pipeline, multi-account structure, and scalable growth.
Schema design for trades, users, accounts, subscriptions, and the AI-extracted trade data, built to scale cleanly as features are added.

Account Switching is the platform's built-in differentiator: a trader can add up to two accounts and flip between them — say, a crypto account and an equity account — without logging in separately or losing either one's journal history. Most single-account journal tools don't offer this out of the box.

Table/list view of all logged trades with filters.
Single-trade view with full details, manual edit, and delete.
Charts and stats — win rate, P&L trends, drawdown, breakdowns.
Ranked list of traders by performance.
Trader's rule-following score and behaviour tracking.
In-app messages and alerts, with resend/unsend.
Screen/modal to add and switch between up to two trading accounts.
Razorpay, UPI, and MetaMask/crypto payment flow.
Admin's overview of platform activity and health.
Admin screen to view, edit, or suspend user accounts.
Admin view to manage billing issues and disputes.
Registered separately by the client. Cloudflare Registrar (at-cost, no markup) is a solid option once ready to move, since hosting is on Cloudflare.
Cloudflare Pages, free tier — unlimited static requests and bandwidth, 500 builds/month, up to 100 custom domains, free SSL and DNS.
Supabase, free tier — 500 MB database, 1 GB file storage, 5 GB bandwidth/month, up to 50,000 monthly active users.
Trade screenshots pass through an upload → analyze → delete flow, so storage cost stays close to zero — the extracted data is what's kept permanently, in Supabase.

Transactional email (Resend/Brevo), error monitoring (Sentry), analytics (Cloudflare Web Analytics), legal pages, periodic manual backups, and an optional business email — all covered by free tiers at launch.
Optional additions worth considering to differentiate this from existing trading-journal platforms (Tradervue, TradesViz, etc.):
Let users connect Zerodha, Binance, MT4/5, and other broker APIs so trades sync automatically instead of relying only on screenshot uploads.
Turn the Discipline Board into a single trust score using the anomaly data already being captured.
Unified portfolio view that auto-converts every trade to the user's home currency using live FX rates.
Let traders replay past trades against real price data to see what a different entry/exit would have done to their P&L.
Leaderboard badges backed by synced broker data, so rankings can't be faked with edited screenshots.
Auto-generate a shareable, Instagram-story-style trade card for social posting.
One-click P&L and F&O statements formatted for Indian tax filing.
Stop-loss and overtrading alerts based on Discipline Board patterns.
Live fraud/anomaly monitoring view in the Admin Panel.
Support staff vs. finance vs. super-admin roles inside the Admin Panel.
Let crypto users link a wallet address so trades can be pulled directly on-chain.
Support more than one crypto wallet per user.
More than two accounts as a paid add-on for power users trading across several brokers.

Design a modern, data-forward fintech dashboard for an AI-powered trading journal. The tone is calm, precise, and trustworthy — closer to a professional charting terminal than a consumer app, but still approachable for retail traders. Favour clarity over decoration: every screen should let numbers and trends read at a glance. Dark mode is the primary experience (traders often work at night and alongside charting tools), with a fully-designed light mode as an equal alternative, not an afterthought.
12-column responsive grid, generous 24–32px gutters, content max-width ~1280px on desktop, single-column stacking below 768px.
Persistent left sidebar (collapsible to icons-only) for primary navigation; a slim top bar for account switcher, notifications, and search.
Everything lives in cards — 12–16px corner radius, 1px hairline border, soft elevation shadow (avoid heavy drop shadows). Cards get consistent 20–24px internal padding.
Table-heavy screens (Trade History, Admin) use compact row height with clear zebra striping; dashboard widgets use looser spacing to let charts breathe.

A clean geometric/grotesque sans — Inter, Manrope, or IBM Plex Sans — for UI text; a tabular-figure numeric font (e.g. Inter with tabular-nums) for all monetary and percentage values so columns of numbers align.
Modest type scale: 13px captions, 14px body, 16px section labels, 20–24px card/page headings, 28–32px hero/landing headings. Bold weight reserved for emphasis, not default body text.

A restrained neutral base (near-black ink on near-white in light mode; deep navy-black on off-white text in dark mode) lets a single confident brand blue carry all primary actions and links. Green and red are reserved exclusively for profit/loss and trend direction, so their meaning never gets diluted by decorative use elsewhere. Amber marks anomalies and discipline warnings. See the palettes in Sections 11–12 for exact values.
Solid primary-blue for main actions, ghost/outline for secondary, subtle scale + shadow-lift on hover, 8px corner radius.
Line and candlestick charts with thin 1.5–2px strokes, soft area-fill gradients fading to transparent, gridlines at 8–10% opacity, profit/loss colour-coded automatically.
Pill-shaped, low-opacity tinted background with full-opacity text in the matching semantic colour (success/danger/warning/info).
Skeleton loaders matching final layout shape; friendly, minimal illustrations for empty states (no trades yet, no flags, etc.).
Fast, subtle transitions (150–200ms ease-out) — fade/slide for panels, no bouncy or playful easing; this is a tool for focus, not delight-driven marketing.

Outline-style icon set (Lucide or Phosphor), 1.5–2px stroke weight, consistently sized at 18–20px in UI chrome and 24px for feature highlights. Avoid photographic imagery inside the app; use abstract gradient mesh or chart-line motifs on marketing/landing surfaces only.
Default background is a soft off-white (not pure white) so card surfaces stand out without heavy borders.
Primary buttons, links, active nav item, key data highlights, focus rings.
Headings, logo mark, high-emphasis text, sidebar background.
Premium/AI features, badges, secondary CTAs, subtle gradients.
Dividers, card outlines, table borders, input borders.

Profitable trades, positive P&L, success toasts, upward trend lines.
Losing trades, negative P&L, destructive actions, error states.

Backgrounds sit in the navy-black family rather than true black, which keeps long dashboard sessions easier on the eyes and lets shadows and elevation still read. Primary, accent, and info hues are lightened versions of their light-mode counterparts to maintain AA contrast on dark surfaces; success, danger, and warning are similarly brightened.
